# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for answering detailed questions)

## BOOK 1 of 2: LORD STRANLEIGH ABROAD (Robert Barr, Ward, Locke & Co., 1913; Gutenberg #32185)
Contents: I Lord Stranleigh All at Sea (p7); II An Automobile Ride (49); III The God in the Car (87); IV The Mad Miss Maturin (125); V In Search of Game (164); VI The Bunk House Prisoner (209); VII The End of the Contest (259). Frontispiece: "'Why did you wish to murder me?'" (p.189).

**Main characters:** Edmund Trevelyan = Lord Stranleigh of Wychwood (alias Trevelyan, later "Henry Johnson", "Edmund Stranleigh"); valet Ponderby (dislikes America, disapproves of democracy; ~37 new suits; later posed as the "gentleman" with Stranleigh as his chauffeur); Hon. John (Jack) Hazel, ruined gambler, expelled from Camperdown Club, alias William Jones on steerage ticket, cabin 4390; Doctor (ship's medical officer, friend, seats Stranleigh at right-hand of his table); Charles Branksome / "Branksome Poole" (blackmailer, ex-chauffeur, forger, gambler, wife's abuser); Mrs. Branksome Poole (distant Trevelyan relative, lost purse, Stranleigh lent £100); Wentworth Parkes (fake Sterling motor man, ex-valet of Duke of Rattleborough, bolted with things); Duke of Rattleborough (letter-writer, cabled "Letter a forgery..."); J.E. Sterling (young Detroit engineer, Woodbridge Street shop, "safety pegs" device); Challis (James/Jim Challis, engineer, married Gertrude Anson); Gertrude Challis (daughter of Stanmore Anson); Stanmore Anson (old mill owner, Anson's Mill, Swedish ancestry, bankrupt, the Trust); Mrs. Anson; Asa Perkins (Boston friend, house); Langdon, Bliss & Co. (Challis's firm); Edward "Ned" Trenton (Pennsylvania coal/rail magnate, Philadelphia); Mrs. Vanderveldt (Trenton's sister, husband scholarly ex-Minister to Italy); Constance Maturin (Miss Maturin, heiress, junior partner, model city on heights above Powerville; John L. Boscombe rival; dam built by her father); Boscombe (reputed millionaire, calls her mad); Banks (John L. Banks, Ice Trust attorney, NY); Stanley Armstrong (ranch owner, silver mine, Chicago, tramping home); Mrs. Armstrong; Miss Armstrong (Dr. Armstrong, medicine professor, Lausanne, cook trained at Thun); Jim Dean (leader of six rancher "partners", shot Stranleigh's left shoulder; Stranleigh shot his ear); Silas A. Ricketts (Bleachers lawyer, sheriff's ally); Timmins (lawyer); Detective Burns (NY, Stranleigh telegraphs); Erasmus Blank (millionaire blackmailed by Poole).

**Key events in order:**
- Ch I: Trevelyan boards liner at Southampton (Cherbourg, Queenstown, NY). Meets doctor. Meets Hazel (3rd class). Stranleigh gives Hazel cabin 4390 (£ via purser; steerage ticket for William Jones). Dinner-table. Stranleigh gives £100 (two £50 notes) to a young woman, Miss Trevelyan, lost purse. Next evening Poole, claiming to be her husband, demands money; Ponderby ejects him. Mrs. Poole tells story (married secretly, father Stanmore?—father went to America motor tour, Branksome was chauffeur; father died, cut her off). Stranleigh arranges detention by wireless. Poole cheats at cards with Hazel (who had the two £50 notes); caught; Poole detained.
- Ch II: Stranleigh in NY, reporters; moves hotels under names; Parkes pursues, sells option on Sterling Motor Co. (Detroit, $100,000). Stranleigh test-drives; Rattleborough cable reveals Parkes was forgery-holder and valet. Stranleigh sails via Canada (St. John NB); settles as "Henry Johnson" in Detroit. Meets J.E. Sterling in Woodbridge Street shop; buys option ($500 deposit, then $500 more). Parkes chauffeurs; attempts blackmail on Canadian road by Lake St. Clair; Stranleigh hurls him into river. Stranleigh gives Parkes $500 + $500 via Sterling.
- Ch III: Stranleigh as chauffeur for Ponderby (Altonville, furnished house; $15,000 credited to Ponderby at Altonville bank). Passes young couple near lake; picks up Challis (husband) and Mrs. Challis (sprained ankle), doctor in Altonville. Challis's story: consultant for Langdon, Bliss & Co.; reports on Anson's mill; Anson's letter; Challis fired; married Gertrude. Anson's mill at auction (Seventeenth of November; bankruptcy court). Stranleigh buys mill and ten acres from Anson for named sum; Challis appointed manager. Gertrude reunited with father ("Shall we throw our differences on that scrap-heap?").
- Ch IV: Ned Trenton (Philadelphia, lakes/dams, "conservation"). Constance Maturin's dam on Trenton river (father's). Trenton dynamited dam earlier; lawsuit. Sis = Mrs. Vanderveldt. Stranleigh rides with Constance (six-cylinder car); conversation: "We have no plans." Stranleigh offers money; she plans model city; asks him to buy Powerville stock; Boscombe blocks; "Blow Boscombe". Dam bursts during festival (cloud-burst), flood destroys valley town and mills. Boscombe: "This is murder!" Stranleigh: "Whoever is responsible ... should be hanged!"
- Ch V: NY Fifth Avenue; University Club; Banks (Ice Trust) recommends Stanley Armstrong's ranch; Stranleigh travels to Bleachers station; guide and mules; shot in left shoulder by Jim Dean at trail edge; guide and escort abandon luggage. Stranleigh goes to house; Mrs. Armstrong, then Miss Armstrong (Dr.) dresses wound. Jim Dean admits he shot to nip him. Miss Armstrong's debt explanation: father borrowed $5,000 from Ricketts (note on demand; ranch security); Armstrong in Chicago; sale in two weeks. Stranleigh offers to lend $2,000 + $3,000 (total $5,000 to pay Ricketts); she accepts.
- Ch VI: Stranleigh explores mine (cavern, dynamite at end, waterfall 100 ft); Jim and three others warn him off west of farmhouse; Stranleigh tells Miss Armstrong; rides to Bleachers; sees Ricketts ($5 fee); telegraph operator; Ricketts offers operator $1; Stranleigh sends telegram to NY (Burns) and Pinkerton-style message; sends for $20,000 cash by express. Dean follows him; Stranleigh captured at dusk; locked in bunk house (six bunks; stone walls; door guarded). Stranleigh notes fireplace/chimney soot.
- Ch VII: Stranleigh climbs chimney, takes rifle, food, builds dynamite-wall barricade at mine mouth; shoots Jim's left ear (perforates "S" on door). Parley; armistice; Jim bandaged ear (Miss Armstrong). Stranleigh tells "Armstrong" and Miss Armstrong; discovers handkerchief with crest (Jim's ear). Stranleigh meets Armstrong on road; hires men as bodyguard ($50 each; six bills); buys ranch at auction for $17,000 (Ricketts's bid $16,000 fails; sheriff). Gives ranch deed to Miss Armstrong as medical bill payment (plus Jim's bill); she says "Good-bye to you, Lord Stranleigh of Wychwood"; she recognised him from NY paper and crest/monogram.

## BOOK 2 of 2: ADVENTURES OF BINDLE (Herbert Jenkins; Gutenberg #32285)
Dedication: "To the Children of the Dead End." Chapters: I The Coming of the Lodger (9); II A Downing Street Sensation (20); III The Air-Raid (35); IV The Duplication of Mr. Hearty (41); V The Gathering of the Bands (50); VI Mr. Gupperduck's Mishap (61); VII The Courting of the Rev. Andrew MacFie (69); VIII The Chapel Conversazione (80); IX The Letting of Number Six (95); X The Downfall of Mr. Jabez Stiffson (105); XI The Camouflaging of Mr. Gupperduck (117); XII The Tragedy of Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino (123); XIII The Return of Charlie Dixon (135); XIV Mr. Hearty Yields (142); XV A Billeting Adventure (150); XVI Millie's Wedding (162).

**Characters:** Joseph "Joe" Bindle (furniture remover, special constable, Fulham, Fenton Street; cricket cap; "Ole Joe"; wife Lizzie/Mrs. Bindle, religious, Gospel Sentinel); Alfred "Alf" Hearty (greengrocer, Putney, pompous, "Earty"; shops: Putney High Street, three shops; "Pineapple Alf"; wife Martha Hearty, wheezes, breath); Millie (Millikins) Hearty (niece, sweetheart Sgt. Charles "Charlie" Dixon, 110th Service Bn London Regt.); Josiah Gupperduck (lodger, accordion, Society for Suppression of Atheism, red nose, ears like signboards); Ginger (friend, spits, "I don't 'old wiv" war/twins); Wilkes (coughs constantly; ~12–18 children); Huggles (friend, "Uggles"); Tippitt (weedy carter, cigarette); Spotty; Scratcher (waiter); Ruddy Bill; Horace Gaze; Lady Knob-Kerrick (Barton Bridge, The Poplars, Putney Hill; footman John; Miss Strint companion; Mr. Wilton butler; Mrs. Marlings); Rev. Andrew MacFie (Scottish minister, Alton Road Chapel; sister Miss MacFie); Rev. Mr. Sopley (retiring); Dick Little, Tom Little, "Guggers" (Captain, Gordons); Nancy Dane (Pierrette); Llewellyn John (PM, 110 Downing St); Chief-Inspector Gunny; Mr. Stiffson / Jabez Stiffson (with canary Oscar); Mrs. Stiffson; Cissie Boye (actress, "Kiss Me Quick", Regent Theatre); Charlie Hart (porter, Fulham Square Mansions); Mrs. Sedge ("Royal Richard" gin); Number Seven (ex-Indian civil servant); Queenie (maid, Number Eight); Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino (Napolini's waiter, Regent Street); James Smith / Herr Siegesmann (chief superintendent); Mr. Black (groceries); Alice (maid), Bertha; Mr. Pain, Mr. Withers, Mr. Gash, Mr. Tuddenham, Mr. Muskett, Miss Torkington.

**Key events in order:**
- Ch I: Mrs. Bindle answers ad "CHRISTIAN HOME wanted... Apply Lonely, c/o The Gospel Sentinel". Mr. Josiah Gupperduck arrives (Monday), accordion, temperance; Bindle's remarks on "pleasant for the ducks". Bindle hears Horace Gaze story. Mrs. Bindle's humiliation. Ch I ends with Bindle's warning ("it's got to be 'ands orf my missis").
- Ch II: Bindle rides horse (Tippitt) to Merton for Empson & Daley delivering carved-oak dining-room furniture to Mr. Llewellyn John, 110 Downing Street. Van holds suffragettes (Black and White Raiders). Bindle perforates van roof, pumps lamp-black; inspector cooperates; raiders dumped in Whitehall. Chief-Inspector Gunny gives praise; Bindle awarded Deputy-Commissioner's cigar.
- Ch III: Air-raid. Mr. Hearty and Gupperduck hide in potato-cellar; Bindle drops scales to trap them; Mrs. Bindle faints in cellar. "All Clear" signal. Millie: "Uncle Joe... only Uncle Joe I've got."
- Ch IV: Mrs. Bindle's jealousy; Hearty opens third shop (Putney High Street). Bindle plans with Dick Little, Guggers for publicity rag. Bindle's "Six Alibis": six duplicates of Mr. Hearty appear; Hearty says "Joseph, I give these men in charge."
- Ch V: Bands gather at Hearty's shop: donkeys with boards ("ALFRED HEARTY, THE NAPOLEON OF GREENGROCERS," "HEARTY'S JERUSALEM ARTICHOKES... GENERAL ALLENBY EATS THEM," etc.); camel with "I'VE GOT THE HUMP"; ~8 bands (Pull for the Shore, Sailor; Onward Christian Soldiers; Shall We Gather at the River; Gospel Bells; The Last Noel). Inspector arrives; summons.
- Ch VI: Gupperduck injured at a Peace meeting in Hyde Park (wounded soldiers); tree-climbing man (Peter/Wayskin? "Mr. Wayskin"); Mrs. Bindle nurses Gupperduck; Bindle: "I'll camelflage 'im."
- Ch VII: Rev. Andrew MacFie courts Millie; Bindle exposes; Hearty nettled. Millie: "I understood."
- Ch VIII: Conversazione at Alton Road school-room; Lady Knob-Kerrick presents Sopley's gifts; glee-party sings "The Glad Eye"; woman "Calves"/Mrs. Calves? (MacFie's wife claimant) — Bindle's "Calves" and Alice; John blows police-whistle; false raid; MacFie denounced; L20 advertisement.
- Ch IX: Bindle minds Fulham Square Mansions for Charlie Hart; Number Six let to Jabez Stiffson (double-booked with Cissie Boye); Oscar the canary; Bindle wears special's uniform.
- Ch X: Stiffson in bath; Cissie Boye; Mrs. Stiffson arrives; bowl of porridge smashed on Stiffson's head; lift stuck; Bindle reassures.
- Ch XI: Gupperduck injured at Hyde Park/peace meeting; Mrs. Bindle nurses him; Bindle says he'll "camouflage" him.
- Ch XII: Bindle works as waiter at Napolini's (Regent Street). Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino (Italian waiter) attacks Bindle; spy documents found; arrested (Defence of the Realm Act). Herr Smith ("Berlice!").
- Ch XIII: Charlie Dixon returns on leave; proposes; Bindle persuades Hearty; Millie marries Charlie.
- Ch XIV: Bindle threatens Hearty with blackmail about past; Hearty consents to wedding ("Toosday").
- Ch XV: Bindle and Ginger, Wilkes, Huggles deliver 16 bedsteads to Lady Knob-Kerrick's drawing-room; soldiers arrive; Lady K. refuses; Bindle's "various veins" line.
- Ch XVI: Millie's wedding at Alton Road Chapel; Sopley officiates (gloomy); Mr. Dixon (Charlie's uncle, "Beer!"); Bindle's speech; Bindle and Dixon pursue taxi to Putney Bridge; Mrs. Dixon thanks Bindle.
